Motorcycle Helmet Safety Ratings Explained

Understanding helmet safety ratings is crucial for every rider. This guide compares the two main UK standards: ECE 22.06 (the mandatory EU certification) and the SHARP rating (independent UK government crash testing).

ECE 22.06

The current European standard, mandatory for all helmets sold for road use in the UK. Tests include impact absorption at multiple points, retention system strength, visor optical quality, and rotational impact resistance. Look for the ECE label inside the helmet.

SHARP Rating

The UK government's Safety Helmet Assessment and Rating Programme independently crash-tests helmets and awards a 1–5 star rating. A 4 or 5 star SHARP rating gives excellent real-world confidence in your helmet's crash protection.

What to Look For

  • ECE 22.06 sticker inside the helmet
  • SHARP 4–5 star rating recommended
  • Correct fit — no pressure points
  • Pinlock-ready visor for UK conditions
Warning: Never buy a second-hand helmet — you cannot see internal damage from previous impacts.
keyTakeaways: ECE 22.06 is the current mandatory European standard for road-legal helmets in the UK.
SHARP is the UK government's independent crash-test rating from 1 to 5 stars.
Aim for a SHARP 4 or 5 star rating for excellent real-world crash protection.
Check for the ECE 22.06 label inside the helmet before you buy.
Never buy a second-hand helmet, as internal impact damage is invisible.

faq.q: What is the difference between ECE 22.06 and SHARP?
faq.a: ECE 22.06 is a mandatory pass/fail certification that every road-legal helmet sold in the UK must meet, testing impact absorption, retention, visor quality and rotational forces. SHARP is a separate, voluntary UK government programme that crash-tests helmets and awards one to five stars, giving you a comparative measure of real-world protection.

faq.q: Is a SHARP 5-star helmet always better than a 3-star one?
faq.a: A higher SHARP rating indicates better performance in the crash tests, so a 4 or 5 star helmet is a strong choice. That said, fit matters just as much as the rating. A perfectly fitting 3-star helmet can protect you better in practice than a loose 5-star one, so always prioritise correct fit alongside the score.

faq.q: Do I legally need a SHARP rating to ride in the UK?
faq.a: No. UK law requires only that your helmet meets an approved standard such as ECE 22.06 and carries the correct label. SHARP is an independent guide to help you choose a safer helmet, not a legal requirement. Use it as a useful extra layer of information when comparing models within your budget.

faq.q: Why should I never buy a second-hand helmet?
faq.a: A helmet's protective shell and liner can be compromised by impacts or drops that leave no visible external damage. You cannot see whether a used helmet has been dropped or crashed, and degraded materials will not protect you properly. Buy new, and replace your own helmet after any significant impact.

faq.q: What features matter for UK riding conditions?
faq.a: Beyond the safety ratings, a Pinlock-ready visor is invaluable for preventing fogging in cool, damp British weather. Good ventilation, a secure retention system, and a comfortable fit with no pressure points all matter. Try several helmets on and wear each for a few minutes to check for hot spots before buying.
